insights.headline: Gold holds above $4,100 into Dhanteras as US settle caps a two-day rally
insights.summary: Spot gold held near $4,123 after touching a two-week high of $4,146, and front-month gold settled 1% higher at $4,102.50 in New York as yields and the dollar eased. In Delhi, gold climbed Rs 2,200 to Rs 1.48 lakh per 10 g ahead of Dhanteras, with jewellers expecting about 75 tonnes of sales. Uday Kotak expects the RBI to raise rates by another 50-75 basis points after its first increase this year, while the rupee closed at 94.47, its strongest since October 21, ahead of Friday's US payrolls report at 7 PM IST.
points: MCX gold jumped Rs 6,500 per 10 g in two days and silver Rs 11,200 per kg as a softer dollar and lower yields lifted bullion after the US midterms.
Front-month gold settled 1% higher at $4,102.50 in New York, the highest settlement since October 21, with silver at $52.23 an ounce.
Jewellers expect a busy Dhanteras with about 75 tonnes of sales as advance bookings rise and buyers favour coins, bars and lightweight jewellery.
Uday Kotak expects the RBI to raise rates by another 50-75 bps, warning tightening is weighing on long-term bonds, as oil risks widen the deficit.
The rupee closed at 94.47, its strongest since October 21, while the 10-year bond yield fell to 7.17%; US October payrolls land Friday at 7 PM IST.

trending.title: Gold holds two-week high into Dhanteras
trending.summary: A softer dollar and easier yields lifted bullion after the US midterms, and Delhi gold reached Rs 1.48 lakh per 10 g on the eve of Dhanteras.

trending.title: Central banks split: buying surges, Russia sells
trending.summary: Central-bank gold buying jumped 42% in the third quarter, the World Gold Council said, while Russia remained the biggest seller of reserves.

trending.title: Silver's breakout watch
trending.summary: Silver held near $53 an ounce with analysts watching a $53.53 breakout level, while Indian silver jumped Rs 11,200 per kg in two days.

trending.title: Dhanteras eve: high prices, lighter pieces, duty-gap risk
trending.summary: Jewellers expect festive sales to rise 20-30% by value as buyers favour lighter pieces, while high import duty pushes some buying to informal channels.

trending.title: What to watch: US payrolls on Friday
trending.summary: The October US jobs report lands Friday at 7 PM IST; a strong print would firm December rate-rise odds, a weak one could ease them. Markets price an 83% chance of a December rise.

items.title: Gold prices jump Rs 6,500/10 gram in 2 days; silver soars Rs 11,200/kg as soft dollar, fall oil boost mood
items.summary: MCX gold added about Rs 6,400 per 10 g and silver about Rs 11,231 per kg over two sessions, with December gold futures at Rs 1,45,909 per 10 g, the Economic Times reports. Spot gold rose 1.9% to $4,134.83 an ounce, its highest since October 22, and spot silver 1.7% to $53.12, as a weaker dollar, falling US yields and crude oil down about 10% followed the Democrats' midterm sweep.

items.title: Jewellers expect fall in gold prices to boost Dhantera sales
items.summary: Jewellers expect a busy Dhanteras as the recent fall in gold prices lifts demand, with advance bookings rising and coins, bars and lightweight hallmarked jewellery leading sales; the trade body estimates about 75 tonnes of sales, and one large jeweller reports enquiries up 40–50% since prices eased.

items.title: Gold Settles Higher As Yields, U.S. Dollar Weaken
items.summary: Front-month gold settled 1% higher in New York at $4,102.50 an ounce, the highest settlement since October 21, as yields and the dollar lost ground, the Wall Street Journal reports. Silver gained 0.2% to $52.233 an ounce.

items.title: Gold hits a two-week high as dollar, Treasury yields ease after US midterm elections
items.summary: Spot gold rose 1.9% to $4,134.83 an ounce on Thursday, its highest since October 22, as a weaker dollar and lower Treasury yields followed the Democrats' midterm sweep, Reuters reports. December futures rose 1.8% to $4,144.20 and spot silver rose 1.7% to $53.12. Traders await Friday's payrolls, pricing an 82% chance of a December Fed rise, per CME FedWatch.

items.title: Gold market holding solid gains even as BoE raises interest rates due to rising inflation
items.summary: The Bank of England raised its Bank Rate by 0.25 points to 4% as UK inflation runs hot, yet gold held its gains, with spot gold up 1.74% at $4,128.54 an ounce.

items.title: Ahead of Dhanteras, gold prices climb Rs 2,200 to Rs 1.48 lakh/10gm in Delhi
items.summary: Gold climbed Rs 2,200 to Rs 1.48 lakh per 10 g in Delhi ahead of Dhanteras, as festive buying picked up on the eve of the festival.

items.title: Why gold and silver prices surged up to 6% in just two sessions and what lies ahead
items.summary: Spot gold bounced from a one-year low of $3,874 an ounce to an intra-week high of $4,146 in two sessions around the US midterms, while silver rose from $48.90 to $53.50. Upstox attributes the rally to a sliding dollar, falling bond yields and central-bank buying, with 321 tonnes bought in the third quarter.

items.title: Gold stalls below $4,150 as US Dollar regains ground, US jobs data in focus
items.summary: Spot gold stalled below $4,150, trading near $4,119 after an intraday high of $4,146, as the dollar and Treasury yields regained ground after the midterm-driven slide. Attention now turns to US jobless claims later on Thursday and the October payrolls report on Friday, which could shape expectations for the Fed’s next move.

items.title: Fed's Hammack Repeats Call for Small Rate Increases to Curb Inflation
items.summary: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack repeated her call for smaller, more frequent rate increases to bring inflation back to 2%, saying policy still needs to tighten; she was one of two officials who dissented in favour of a hike when the Fed held rates last week, and markets price an 83% chance of a December increase, according to CME FedWatch.

items.title: Rupee hits over one-month high, 10-year bond yield falls to 7.17%
items.summary: The rupee closed at 94.47 against the dollar, its strongest since October 21, gaining for a fifth straight session as easing crude prices lifted sentiment, while the 10-year government bond yield fell to 7.17%, its lowest since September 29.

items.title: Titan shines in Q2 Results 2026; Net profit doubles to  ₹2,393 crore, aided by one-time gain; jewellery business up 24%
items.summary: Titan's net profit doubled to Rs 2,393 crore in the September quarter, helped by a one-time gain, with its jewellery business up 24% as festive demand held up despite record prices.

items.title: Reserve Bank of India may hike rates by up to 75 bps more: Uday Kotak
items.summary: Uday Kotak expects the RBI to raise the repo rate by another 50-75 basis points after its first increase this year, warning the tightening is weighing on long-term bonds, Business Standard reports. He cited prolonged West Asia risks and sharply higher oil, and noted India's deficit was only $26 billion in 2025-26 even after $72 billion of gold imports.

items.title: Gold Prices On Recovery Mode: Yellow Metal Rates Jump By Rs 6,600 In Two Days To Rs 1,46,100
items.summary: MCX December gold futures rose to Rs 1,46,109 per 10 g, up Rs 6,657 in two sessions from Rs 1,39,452 on November 3, NDTV Profit reports. COMEX gold futures moved up to nearly $4,147, gaining 1.83% after a 3.6% jump on Wednesday, as the dollar stayed weak after the Democrats' midterm sweep.

items.title: Russia leads global gold reserve sell-off amid war costs
items.summary: Russia remained the world's biggest seller of central-bank gold, selling about 62 tonnes from its reserves over ten months to plug a widening budget deficit — the fastest sell-off since the 1998 crisis.

Central banks bought ~320 tonnes in Q3, up 42% on the year and ~675t so far in 2026, the WGC said — offsetting a 17% slump in jewellery consumption to ~310t, the weakest Q3 in the series, and a 19% fall in bar and coin demand. Gold averaged ~$4,260/oz; total demand was ~1,370t (-1%), with YTD demand level with 2025’s record.
items.title: Central bank gold buying jumps 42% in Q3 as high prices hit jewellery demand, WGC says
'Gold's rally is not just about wars, it's fundamentally linked to $40 tn US debt': WGC India CEO Sachin Jain
items.summary: World Gold Council India CEO Sachin Jain said gold's rally is fundamentally linked to the $40 trillion US debt pile, not just wars, arguing that fiscal strain underpins demand for the metal.

items.title: Dhanteras Gold Buyers Turn To Informal Channels As Import Duty Fuels Smuggling
items.summary: A LocalCircles survey found 29% of planned Dhanteras gold buyers may use informal channels, as the 15% import duty plus GST lifts the total levy to about 18.45%. The World Gold Council put unofficial inflows at about 50 tonnes in July-September, up from about 3 tonnes a year earlier.

items.title: Gold Futures Rise To Rs 1.45 Lakh/10 Gm On Firm Spot Demand; Silver Futures Decline
items.summary: MCX December gold futures rose Rs 1,947 to Rs 1,45,181 per 10 g on firm spot demand, while December silver futures eased Rs 28 to Rs 1,87,707 per kg, PTI reports via ETV Bharat. Gold futures in New York rose 1.24% to $4,110.88 an ounce, while silver globally slipped 0.56% to $52.51.

items.title: MCX Q2 profit jumps over two-fold to ₹455 crore as trading volumes surge
items.summary: MCX reported a more than two-fold rise in September-quarter net profit to Rs 455 crore from Rs 197.47 crore a year ago, as total income more than doubled to Rs 799.66 crore. Average daily futures turnover rose to Rs 62,819 crore, and the exchange delivered 5.68 tonnes of gold and 199.91 tonnes of silver in the quarter.

Silver is testing downtrend resistance from late-September highs after reclaiming $51.27 and $52.67, with gold's breakout from its own September downtrend lighting the way, FOREX.com's technical analysis says. The metals' 10-day correlation is +0.99 with silver's beta near 1.7, so a confirmed breakout could target $54.78-$58.50; $51.27-$52.67 must hold, with $48.86 the key support below.
items.title: Silver's bullish breakout case builds as bond yields retreat
Silver at a Critical Crossroads: $53.53 Breakout Could Ignite the Next Rally
items.summary: Silver futures traded near $52.76, up about 0.91% on the session, with immediate resistance at $53.01 and then $53.53, Investing.com's technical analysis notes. Support sits at $51.25, with $50.00 below that, as the metal tests the top of its recent range.

Spot gold climbed 3% to $4,046.74 an ounce on Wednesday — its biggest daily gain since August 19 — as the dollar slid after Democrats swept both chambers of Congress in the midterms. December gold futures rose 2.9% to $4,054.60. Capital Economics' Hamad Hussain said fiscal worries supported bullion, but a likely hawkish Fed could cap gains, with Friday's US payrolls report the next test.
items.title: Gold gains 3% as dollar slides after Democratic midterm gains
US October Nonfarm Payrolls Preview: Can Employment Rebound? US Stocks, Dollar and Gold Face Key Test
items.summary: The US October jobs report lands on Friday, November 6, with markets expecting about 65,000 jobs, up from 29,000 in September, and unemployment steady at 4.2%, TradingKey reports. The Fed held rates at 3.75-4.00% in October while markets still price about an 80% chance of a December hike; a strong print would reinforce that, a weak one could shift rate expectations and move the dollar and gold.

items.title: BIS Hallmarking System Strengthens Consumer Trust, Over 65 Crore Gold Articles Get HUID
items.summary: More than 65 crore gold articles have been hallmarked with a unique HUID since mandatory hallmarking began, the Bureau of Indian Standards said, as buyers check purity ahead of Dhanteras.

Mandatory BIS hallmarking does not apply to gold articles under 2 grams, traditional Kundan, Polki and Jadau jewellery, or gold watches and fountain pens, Zee Business reports. Gold bullion in bars, plates and other forms is also exempt, as are export and medical-use articles, though jewellers may still pass on the Rs 75-per-article hallmarking fee.
items.title: Buying gold for Dhanteras and Diwali 2026? Check which jewellery is exempt from mandatory hallmarking
NSE EGR Trading: Exchange expects higher activity on Dhanteras; 2,781 trades recorded so far
items.summary: NSE's Electronic Gold Receipt platform expects higher activity on Dhanteras, with 2,781 trades recorded so far as more buyers turn to demat gold.

items.title: US Midterm Election Results Impact on Gold, Silver Jewellery Stocks: Senco, PC, Titan shares shine on Trump's loss
items.summary: Jewellery stocks rose as bullion rebounded, Mint reports: Senco Gold gained 3.7% to Rs 322.65, PC Jeweller 3.2% to Rs 16.32, Titan 2.3% to Rs 4,858.90 and Kalyan 2.7% to Rs 544.70. MCX gold traded at Rs 1,46,109 per 10 g and silver at Rs 1,90,946 per kg, with spot gold at $4,134.83 an ounce, as a weaker dollar and lower Treasury yields followed the Democrats' midterm win.

Jewellers are upbeat on Dhanteras sales on November 6 after gold's 12% price correction lifted sentiment, GJC chairman Rajesh Rokde told PTI. Demand is shifting to lightweight jewellery and small-ticket purchases, while silver coins gain traction with a 10% volume rise expected. Sales volumes should stay flat, but in value terms the industry expects about 30% growth.
items.title: Why Jewellers Expect Strong Dhanteras Sales Amid Recent Gold Price Drop
Gold vs silver this Dhanteras: Price outlook, buying trends and key risks
items.summary: CNBC-TV18 weighs gold against silver for Dhanteras buyers: gold is about 20% below its January peak and silver roughly 50% below, after silver's much sharper October correction. The piece notes silver's higher volatility and industrial demand, and that lower prices are drawing festive buyers toward lighter gold pieces and silver jewellery.

items.title: Buying gold this Dhanteras? What investors should keep in mind
items.summary: Ahead of Dhanteras on November 6, CNBC-TV18 notes gold prices have corrected and sets out what buyers check before purchasing: purity, BIS hallmarking, weight and making charges. The piece cites US bond yields, the dollar, inflation and geopolitics, plus the rupee and import duties at home, as the forces shaping prices, and quotes MMTC-PAMP on systematic buying.
